quote: I'm reaching out about the solar form you still got online.
stewart_read: Intro references the form but the rep never re-establishes legitimacy given the customer's known prior contact/complaint history — no acknowledgment of the repeat-contact issue up front.
coaching_implication: When a lead has an open complaint about repeat contact, address it directly in the first line rather than a generic form reference.

quote: you guys keep calling me and texting me.
stewart_read: Customer raises a contact-frequency complaint and the rep's only response is a flat 'Okay.' with no acknowledgment or resolution.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged this unresolvable mid-call and prioritized the DQ question instead — but the complaint was never addressed at all, even briefly.
coaching_implication: Acknowledge the complaint briefly ('I hear you, let's get you sorted either way') before moving to qualification — costs 5 seconds, defuses hostility.

quote: I was told that solar will not work on my house
stewart_read: Rep asks a vague version of 'did they say why' but never asks which company/rep, when, or what specifically was shown — schema calls for investigate_first with a clean probe.
coaching_implication: Use the canonical probe 'Do you know why it was disqualified?' cleanly instead of hedging ('I just I'm a little did they say why...').

quote: surface area on the back of the house that doesn't get shade
stewart_read: Customer volunteers detailed roof/HOA constraints (front blocked by HOA, insufficient rear space) that confirm the DQ; rep does not reflect this back or use it to close cleanly, instead pivots straight to a phone-call alternative.
coaching_implication: Reflecting the specifics back ('so the HOA blocks the front and the back doesn't get enough sun — got it') would validate the customer faster and shorten the call before the hold.

quote: I can here. I can help you get a phone call. That way you don't have to sit and meet with anybody and waste your time.
stewart_read: Rep offers an alternative (phone-only appointment) with no anchor on time, value, or reason to say yes — pure deflection attempt that the customer immediately shuts down.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be a genuine attempt to salvage the lead cheaply, but it's unanchored and reactive rather than a considered pivot.
coaching_implication: If offering an alternative channel, tie it to a specific reason ('just to double check with the design team since the map looks clear') rather than a vague low-effort pitch.

quote: So let me ask my manager if you're willing to because you're willing to trim up if it'll work. Just I'll go find out right now.
stewart_read: Rep places the customer on hold to consult a supervisor on a shading/tree-trimming edge case outside standard qualifying flow.
coaching_implication: Correct procedure for a genuine edge case — but the hold ran ~50 seconds with no set-up of what would happen next, risking the customer hanging up.
